summary: Iteration 5 testing complete for the two surgical features (PDF upload + coordinator photo). Backend: 8/8 pytest pass in test_iteration5_pdf.py — /api/admin/upload accepts PDF (max 16MB), still accepts images (max 8MB), rejects .txt with 400, requires admin auth. /api/files/{id} returns application/pdf content-type with %PDF payload. Trip model accepts+persists itinerary_pdf_url on create + update, GET returns it, and all 9 seeded trips have the field (empty string). Frontend: /conocenos coordinator photo loads (naturalWidth=1536, correct URL, Marinerus card overlay present). Admin /admin/trips 'Nuevo viaje' modal renders PdfUploadField with all data-testids (trip-pdf-url, trip-pdf-btn, trip-pdf-file) plus 'Itinerario PDF' label — confirmed visually. End-to-end integration: (a) uploaded a PDF via /api/admin/upload from the browser (cookie session) → 200 with /api/files/{id} url; (b) POST /api/admin/trips with that itinerary_pdf_url → 200; (c) visited /destinos/{id} → 'Descargar itinerario PDF' button (download-itinerary) rendered with correct href to the PDF file. Seed trips (empty pdf) correctly fall back to the day-by-day itinerary blocks (download-itinerary count=0).
critical_code_review_comments: PdfUploadField href in TripDetail uses trip.itinerary_pdf_url directly (e.g. '/api/files/xxx'). Because the ingress serves frontend+backend on the same host, browsers resolve the relative URL to the correct origin — works fine here, but if the app is ever deployed with a separate BACKEND_URL host, the download link would 404. Consider prefixing with BACKEND_URL (as PdfUploadField already does for the 'Ver PDF' preview).

MIME_TYPES accepts pdf but /api/admin/upload validates only by file extension (file.filename.rsplit). No magic-byte check — a malicious admin could upload arbitrary bytes named .pdf. Low risk since endpoint requires admin auth, but worth noting.
Carry-over from prior iterations: init_storage/put_object still sync inside async handlers; server.py still ~900 lines; CORS allow_origin_regex='.*' with credentials=true remains overly permissive.
